Test speed without weaker tests (user decisions 2026-11-08). Measured 2026-11-08 (i9-11900H, g++ 16.2): compiling is 81% of quick-mode time over the 154 contest suites (3,747 s compiling against 870 s running, 8 suites at a time) and exceeds running in 148 of them; about 90% of a slow build is GCC optimization and code generation of the testers' instantiations (`-ftime-report`: 55 s for `18-persistentsegmenttree`), parsing the headers about 2 s. So precompiled headers are ruled out, and so is changing the checked build's `-O0` (`-O1`/`-Og` were faster on `01-dsu` full, slower on `18-persistentsegmenttree` full and in quick mode). Work: (1) Build cache. One shared build helper in `96-Local Testing/_00_cpp_test_runner.py` compiles every translation unit with `-c` through ccache (probed as `02-integration.py` does, `CCACHE_NOHASHDIR=1`, a plain build reported once when ccache is absent or fails the probe) and links with `$CXX`, read with `shlex.split` everywhere; then a full run's pre-flight and main run, and repeated runs of an unchanged suite, compile each distinct build once (probe: a repeated build 4.2 s to 0.09 s, byte-identical binary; a contest tester's `/package` step 5 compiles about 17 times for about 6 distinct builds). Every C++ test build goes through it: the six folder `_00_runner.py` files merge into one shared contest runner whose per-folder differences (the `-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS` stems, oracle callbacks, `extra`, `timeout`) become parameters; the Core runners and self-building Core testers (`_00_foundation_runner.py`, `_05_modint_test_runner.py`, `run_cpp_suite`, `07-infint`, `08-infintmini`, `09-rational`, `16-poly`, `17-polymini`, `18-bitset`, `19-fastio` and any other); `05-extraction.py testers`, whose scratch tree gets stable relative paths so an unchanged extracted source hits; the compile oracles of `00-Tools/04-dependencies_tester.py` and the `05-extraction.py ops` syntax checks (about 2,400 extractions on each of two compilers), both `-fsyntax-only`, which ccache caches, given stable relative names; and the `04-mutation.py` stages, where hits across shards for one mutant's later stages are measured and enabled (ccache `base_dir` or stable shard paths) only if they provably reuse identical input. ccache joins `TOOLS` in `.claude/skills/setup-check/setup_check.py` as optional. Measure the cache footprint of a full library run on g++ and g++-14; if it exceeds the 5 GB default, raise `max_size` in the user's ccache config to it plus headroom (user decision) and record the value and reason. (2) Warnings. Every contest suite compiles with `-Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Werror` (`05-testing.md`, Builds). 68 suites (03-Geometry, 05-Mathematics, 06-Miscellaneous and the five non-`strict` 04-Graphs suites) compile without warning flags today and showed 0 warnings on 2026-11-08 (`-fsyntax-only` on all 68, `-c -O2 -Werror` on four); the `strict` parameter retires. (3) Quick bound (user decision). Each build's quick run takes at most 10 s alone on this machine, written into `05-testing.md` (Layout and modes) and met by every C++ suite, Core included: first a cheaper oracle with the same checks, then smaller quick-mode inputs; full and stress inputs and oracles stay unchanged, and a check that fits only in full moves there. Over 10 s on 2026-11-08: `16-poly` optimized 51 s (its `multivariateCyclic` oracle at `16-poly_tester.cpp:211` reaches N = 34^3 with two vector allocations per pair, about 40 s; the `convolutionLarge` checks at line 195 most of the rest); contest suites, optimized/checked seconds measured 8 at a time: 13-segment_union 1/58, 14-polynomial_algorithms 6/50, 35-subgraph_enumeration 36/36, 16-centroiddecomposition 1/33, 17-treeisomorphism 1/31, 17-numerical_methods 22/27, 17-bitap 1/26, 15-linear_recurrence 2/24, 12-sais 1/24, 12-combinatorics_advanced 2/19, 14-lyndon 0/17, 13-convolution 1/17, 29-planar_graph 0/16, 16-string_matching 1/16, 64-sortedlist 1/16, 29-knapsack_advanced 1/15, 31-radixheap 1/15, 17-waveletmatrix 1/13, 18-editdistance 1/13, 26-trie 1/12, 23-assignment 0/10, 20-continued_fraction 2/10. Remeasure every suite alone, the Core suites first. The shared runners print each build's compile and run seconds, and `01-run.py --mode quick` lists the builds over 10 s as a NOTE, never a failure (`05-testing.md`, Benchmarks: no fixed timing gates across machines). (4) Parallel builds (user decision). Core suites compile up to 3 builds at once, as `19-fastio` does, within their memory cap (a raise only with a recorded reason, `05-testing.md` Memory safety); contest suites stay sequential. (5) No duplicate quick runs (user decision). The pre-flight stays; `/package` step 5, `/finish` step 5, `/prune` and `/restyle` take a full run's `PREFLIGHT ... quick passed` line as the quick run and never run quick separately before full. (6) Mutation. The last stage runs only the configurations the earlier stages did not (contest testers: checked and ASan-UBSan after full optimized), so a survivor has still passed every configuration in full mode. (7) Timeouts. Every run stays within half its timeout under `01-run.py --mode full` load, by a cheaper oracle with the same checks or else a raised limit with its measured reason (35-subgraph_enumeration's ASan-UBSan full run took 311 s beside other work against 180 s; it is recorded timing out under load and passing rerun alone). (8) Validator. `03-consistency.py` runs after every watched edit and shell command and took 22 s idle (55-75 s loaded, P254) against the hook's 60 s; `strip_cpp` (76,892 calls, about half the time, mostly from grab's mini-first `full_only` through `select`) is memoized by input and other results that depend only on file contents are cached, keeping the JSON output byte-identical (compared before and after on this tree and the fixtures); target at most 10 s idle. (9) Tool suites over 10 s in quick (on 2026-11-06: 13-grab 121 s, 04-dependencies 48 s, 08-plan 38 s, 06-site 35 s, 11-mutation 30 s) are profiled and sped up only by exact means (caching, memoization, ccache); no test is removed. (10) Existing tests (user decision 2026-11-08). The work changes the existing testers and runners of other packages, verified ones included. Each changed tester's header evidence document records what changed: its feature-to-test map when a check moves from quick to full, and new latest-run lines (commands, times, peaks). Mutation records name header blobs and stay current; a check moved to full still runs in the full stages. A tester whose owning package is live when P274 reaches it (a worktree or uncommitted changes to its tests, as `plan.py ready` defines) is left until that package lands, then changed. Record before and after times, cold and warm cache, in `96-Local Testing/Docs/00-parallel.md` (its 'No ccache for the suites' limit retires): one contest and one Core tester's quick, full, g++-14 full and stress sequence; `01-run.py --mode quick` and `--mode full` twice each; `05-extraction.py testers`; a mutation campaign on `01-dsu.hpp`; the validator. `05-runner_tester.py`, `11-mutation_tester.py` and the other tool testers cover the shared helper, the cache fallback and the stage change; every suite passes quick, full and g++-14 full afterwards.
